questions.prompt: If another vehicle is following too close, what should a driver do?
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating, don't brake suddenly or speed up. Slow down gradually and give them a chance to pass. Key words: "to pass".

choices.text: Slow down gradually and encourage the other vehicle to pass
Press hard on the brake pedal
Increase speed to 10 km/h above the posted speed limit
Activate the four-way flashers

questions.prompt: According to the law in Alberta, it is the driver's responsibility to ensure that all passengers under what age are properly restrained in the vehicle?
questions.explanation: The driver must make sure every passenger under 16 is wearing a seat belt or is in the correct child seat. Passengers 16 and older are responsible for themselves. Key words: "all passengers".

choices.text: 18 years
24 years
21 years
16 years

questions.prompt: In Alberta, the law requires that seat belts must be worn:
questions.explanation: Alberta law requires seat belts to be worn and properly adjusted at all times while the vehicle is moving.

choices.text: Only while carrying passengers
Properly at all times
Only when driving at highway speeds
Only when driving in the city

questions.prompt: Using the 2-second rule to judge a safe following distance when driving:
questions.explanation: The 2-second rule measures time, not distance, so the gap grows automatically as you go faster and the rule works at any speed. Leave more time in poor road or weather conditions. Key words: "any speed".

choices.text: Is more accurate on rural highways than in urban centres
Is not accurate at speeds greater than 100 km/h
Is accurate at any speed
Is not accurate at speeds lower than 100 km/h

questions.prompt: When a driver is stopping behind another vehicle in traffic:
questions.explanation: Stop far enough back that you could steer around the vehicle ahead without reversing, for example if it stalls. A good guide is being able to see where its rear tires touch the road. Key words: "sufficient space".

choices.text: Keep back approximately 1 metre from the rear bumper of the vehicle ahead
Allow sufficient space to move into another lane without reversing
Remain a minimum of 10 metres from the vehicle ahead
Maintain sufficient space as determined by the 2-second rule

questions.prompt: When travelling in urban areas, drivers should scan the road approximately:
questions.explanation: In urban areas, look about 12 to 15 seconds ahead, roughly one city block, so you can spot hazards early. Key words: "scan the road".

choices.text: 25 to 30 seconds ahead
20 to 30 seconds ahead
12 to 15 seconds ahead
1 to 6 seconds ahead
